question: Can two overlapping submissions to one finite receiver ledger preserve one debit while classifying pre-transaction SQLite BUSY separately from invalid ledger contents?
scope: One fixed checkpoint question, one accepted slot, two trusted local processes and at most one explicit contender retry after holder termination per episode.
domain: Unchanged exact rational checkpoint and arithmetic profiles; original ledger storage engine reused under a new explicit profile and adapter fingerprint.
quantifier: Eight declared scheduled episodes, one legacy control, one non-SQLite file and two directional profile refusals. No exhaustive scheduler, liveness or distributed-system claim.
profile_boundary: New databases store the new profile and the adapter plus all six inherited receiver hashes. Old/new receivers refuse each other's databases. No ledger migration or relabeling occurs.
receiving: Original expected/candidate schema, stored result, one-slot transaction, allowance and commit-uncertainty rules remain. Only the new outer profile and SQLite error classification change. No automatic retry or budget renewal.

sqlite_classification.primary_5_before_transaction: LedgerBusy. Return no authoritative allowance or stored result; do not claim caller question, candidate validity, unchanged global ledger or permission to retry without a separately bounded caller.
sqlite_classification.primary_11_or_26: InvalidLedger; SQLite corruption or non-database indication is distinct from semantic schema/profile rejection.
sqlite_classification.other_or_busy_in_transaction: UnknownStorage, unless the inherited commit-uncertain or cleanup path conservatively requires reconciliation. SQLITE_LOCKED(6) is not automatically retryable BUSY.

diagnostics: Retain exact sqlite_errorcode, sqlite_errorname, primary code, statement and connection transaction flag. Classify numerically, not by message text.
schedule: Explicitly initialize the receiver-owned ledger and retain a full pre-state snapshot.
Start holder through a test-only pipe gate; signal readiness only after BEGIN IMMEDIATE succeeds and before its ledger reads or candidate checks.
Observe holder PID still alive and launch contender against the same existing file.
Contender must finish with pre-transaction BUSY before holder release. Do not read database snapshots while the holder owns its transaction.
Release holder by pipe message, await and reap it, then observe full logical state.
One explicit fresh contender retry obtains a replay, conflict, capacity pause or first commit according to the declared episode; compare complete logical rows and allowance.
episodes: invalid first candidate then valid contender
asymmetric reuse: same key changed payload
legacy_control: Run the unchanged old receiver as contender against an old-profile holder. Record its existing InvalidLedger result on BUSY without rewriting old code, old evidence or its sequential scope.
assumptions: Trusted local SQLite/OS and inherited DELETE/FULL transaction configuration
Coordinator controls pipe handles and holds no database connection during overlap
Gate waiting is inside holder's existing three-second receiver deadline
Supervisor closes pipe handles and terminates/reaps outstanding children on failure
No external task action beyond the local database effect
residuals: No scheduler fairness, starvation, arbitrary concurrent history or distributed exactly-once result
No power-loss or arbitrary COMMIT/IO failure coverage
No hostile storage, authentication or automatic profile migration
No native communicate/Close/free/M6, universality or measured acceleration
